notes: TBox rule edit: ancient Egyptian obelisks are monoliths; the edit makes them stacks of blocks, as modern obelisks such as the Washington Monument are, so the counterfactual is plausible and clearly false. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is stated directly (Wikipedia: ancient obelisks are monolithic) and follows from nothing. No real exceptions among ancient Egyptian obelisks as the dataset uses the class. The three derived queries name obelisks in the prompt as ancient Egyptian obelisks (the Flaminio Obelisk, the obelisk of Senusret I at Heliopolis, the Boboli obelisk), all little written about as objects, so the rule is the only route: determinate. The famous members (the Luxor Obelisk, Cleopatra's Needle) are not asked; the earlier indeterminate queries, their worlds and checks were removed. The negation is worded 'Is it true that ... were not ...?' because two models answered 'No' to 'Is it false that every ...?' for wording, not logic. The near query (Aswan) differs from the new answer and is no premise.
